headline: Executive order directs federal agencies to treat faith-based and community groups equally when handing out federal social service funds.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order deals with equal treatment of faith-based and community organizations under federal law. It generally tells federal agencies that run social service programs not to favor or disfavor groups because they are religious when they compete for federal grants. Groups getting federal money are generally expected to serve people regardless of the person's religion and to keep religious activities separate from the federally funded services. No official summary was provided, so details may be incomplete.

who_it_affects.group: Religious charities and churches that provide social services
who_it_affects.how: They may compete for federal social service grants on the same terms as non-religious groups.
They are covered by the same equal-treatment rules when seeking federal funding.

who_it_affects.group: People who use federally funded social services
who_it_affects.how: They may receive help from religious providers but are generally not required to take part in religious activities to get services.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that run social service grant programs
who_it_affects.how: They must follow the order's equal-treatment rules when awarding and managing grants.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed December 12, 2002; executive orders usually take effect when signed.
